decision: Mickey's is a minicab office (D19), superseding D15's pub; D15's siting on Quay Street stands; other pubs remain as buildings, never entered for drink.

Late 1980s to early 1990s, working window 1988 to 1992; late-analog world, no internet, no ordinary mobiles; 1950s or 1970s framing is wrong.

Grounded noir with dry British wit and sparing seaside-postcard smut, never GTA-style satire; photoreal, wet, overcast, grimy Britain; the bar is the Meridian Test; GTA V PS3 retired as a reference bar.

Baseline: Tom Nowak, 32, Mickey's nephew, inherits Mickey's minicab office and a half-dead outfit; loyalists Ron Kirby and Sheila Dunn; three rivals (Agar, the Widow Maureen Jensen, Danny Cammack); the day-life ring.
Tom has never been to the Hook: a stranger to everyone, known only as Mickey's nephew by name.
His life before the Hook is left unsaid: nobody asks and he never tells.
Ada was never a teacher.
Sheila withholds Tom's name until she trusts him; the town's name for him reads out his standing (new owner, Nowak, Tom, Tommy).

Renames: Lena Sheila Dunn, Rocco Ron Kirby, Sam Darren Milner, Mara Carol Ellis, Aldous Vane Geoffrey Agar, Sera Kest Maureen Jensen, Noor Alison Sedman, Elias Philip Danby, Danny Ro Danny Cammack, Tom Novak Tom Nowak, Toma Tommy; old names only internal ids.
Father Emil became Father Brendan Walsh, the Fixer is Keith Garbutt, June's surname is Suddaby.
Alcohol and gambling are out entirely, never shown, served, drunk or spoken of; pubs may exist as places.
words: Alcohol and gambling are out ENTIRELY

decision: Tobacco stays.
Violence stays, including blood and light gore; no torture and no cruelty as spectacle.
Killing is possible, rare, permanent, and the town remembers it forever.
Full period swearing is allowed; no slurs of any kind.
Drugs exist as an off-screen economy: never shown, never used, never a player verb.
No prostitution and no sexual content; seaside-postcard innuendo stays.
No children anywhere: none rendered, in the crowd, dialogue or image prompts; the school stands closed.
Racism and sectarianism may exist as facts about characters, never voiced as slurs, never rewarded.
Religion is present as part of life, never mocked, never a mechanic.
Police are corruptible as individuals, never as a thesis.
The moat (unchangeable): every act exposes seven perceivable slots; five-rung identification ladder with recognition gated by relationship.
Permanent per-NPC memory, never wiped; gossip spreads through schedule intersections.
Live LLM conversations with per-character memory and local voice; the deterministic Core decides every outcome, LLMs classify, never adjudicate.
Pillar: verbs first, talk as the consequence; the player mostly acts, talk is where consequences surface and stays the moat, never the main thing the player does.
words: we don't want a gossip simulator. We want an exciting, immersive, novel game.

decision: Targets: about ten distinct activities per thirty minutes; nothing new for at most about five minutes; talk well under half of play time.

D24: not an open-world sandbox, shooter, driving game, economy simulation or story-first game; anything not feeding perception, memory, gossip or consequence gets the smallest budget that keeps it from looking wrong.
Every brand, band, club, product, weapon and vehicle is fictional; no real people, voices, logos, lyrics, car models; the license allowlist is law.
Engine decided: Unreal (D16); Unity is the legacy reference; the C# Core stays the source of truth.
Narrative survival decided: Tom Nowak, the three acts, three rivals and the empire roster are the baseline per the approved story outline.
A ruling that changing canon edits canon in the same batch, and a DECIDED record on a world fact names the canon lines it changes.
